Technology and Sustainability of Life — Year 6

Investigate strong and stable structures, explore the role of technology in everyday life, and design responsible solutions for a more sustainable future.

🏗️ 12.0 Stability and Strength⚙️ 13.0 Technology🌱 Sustainable Living
🌟

Start Your Science Adventure

🧠 Big Idea (Understanding)

Understanding stability and strength helps us build safe, strong and sustainable structures. Technology makes life easier, but its use comes with responsibilities.

Apply these ideas to everyday structures, tools and technologies while considering safety, materials, energy use and environmental impact.

Learning Standards

Showing 11 of 11 Learning Standards · Years 6

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Identify examples of stable and strong structures in daily life.
  • Describe stability and strength using familiar objects.
  • Compare stable and unstable objects.
  • Differentiate stability from strength through observations.
  • Explain why stability and strength matter in everyday structures.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Give examples of strong and stable structures.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Identify examples of stable and strong structures in daily life.
  • Describe stability and strength using familiar objects.
  • Compare stable and unstable objects.
  • Differentiate stability from strength through observations.
  • Explain why stability and strength matter in everyday structures.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • State the meaning of stability and strength.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Compare objects with different base areas and heights of their centres of gravity.
  • Investigate factors affecting stability.
  • Record and compare observations.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • State examples of strong and stable structures.
  • Outline the meaning of stability and strength.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Investigate how materials and shapes affect structural strength.
  • Record and compare experimental results to identify patterns.
  • Draw conclusions from experimental findings.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Describe factors that affect the strength of a structure.
  • Summarise the importance of strong and stable structures for sustainable life.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Generate ideas about strong and stable structures for sustainable living.
  • Connect safe design with suitable materials, shape and support.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Justify the importance of strong and stable structures for sustainable life.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Plan and design a model structure using recyclable materials.
  • Select suitable materials and shapes.
  • Construct, test and evaluate a model, then suggest improvements.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Create a strong and stable model structure.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Communicate findings through labelled sketches, writing, speech or ICT.
  • Suggest improvements based on testing results.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Communicate creatively about the model's strength and stability and suggest improvements.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Technology applies scientific knowledge to overcome human limitations.
  • Examples include smartphones and computers, cars and trains, washing machines and refrigerators.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • State the meaning of technology and identify examples used in daily life.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Explore development in agriculture and farming, medicine, transport and communication.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Describe the importance of technology and identify developments in different fields.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Advantages: faster communication, easier transport and reduced human effort.
  • Disadvantages: pollution, electronic waste and excessive screen time.
  • Compare smartphones, motor vehicles and electrical appliances; consider effects on people and the environment.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Analyse advantages and disadvantages of technologies and explain effects on daily activities and the environment.

🧠 KNOW · Procedural Facts

  • Compare benefits and limitations, effects on human activities and environmental impacts.
  • Use comparison tables, mind maps and examples with logical reasoning.
  • Suggest responsible practices: save electricity, reduce e-waste, repair and reuse devices, and recycle at appropriate collection centres.
  • Evaluate energy efficiency, environmental impact and long-term usefulness; propose an innovative sustainable technology for a real-life problem.

🎯 Performance Standard (DO)

  • Evaluate the effects of technology on sustainable living and communicate an innovative future technology idea, including its advantages and possible disadvantages.
